clue.text: Trendy adult board game place in the USA

explanation.surface: A fashionable grown-up's board game that turns out to be American.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'trendy adult board game' as one thing to buy; split it into three words and the city appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large city in Illinois, so it is a place in the United States.

clue.text: Old statesman’s company importing wild rice

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder
a firm that imports brings goods inside, so one piece is taken in by another

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
the four letters of rice rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly politician's business has started bringing in wild rice.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; CO opens up to take in the jumbled grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was a Roman orator and politician of the first century BC, an ancient statesman.

clue.text: Enter home quietly removing contents of unit

indicators.note: taking out what is inside leaves only the outside edges of the word

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
the word unit emptied of its middle letters N and I

explanation.surface: Someone slips into a house quietly and clears out a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter' looks like the start of a burglary; it is a verb meaning to key data in, and the rest is simple building.
explanation.definitionFit: To input data is to type it into a computer, which is what entering data means.

clue.text: Novel, we hear, about university detective and bespectacled bachelor – not bad!

blocks.note: a. is a less common abbreviation for about
U is the usual abbreviation for university
DI is a Detective Inspector
B for bachelor with an O on each side, like two round lenses
something OK is not bad, just acceptable

explanation.surface: A campus mystery novel about a detective and a bookish bachelor, and it is apparently quite good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' is not a sound-alike signal here but part of the definition: a novel you listen to. The glasses are drawn as two Os round the B.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiobook is a recorded reading, so a novel in that form is one people listen to rather than read.

clue.text: Rotten, worthless and wrong in 1A

blocks.note: food that has gone off is rotten
base metal is the low-value kind, so base means worthless

explanation.surface: A grim verdict on something bad and mistaken in Chicago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In 1A' points to the answer at 1 across, CHICAGO, standing for America: off base is a US phrase from baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A baserunner caught off base is out, so in American idiom off base means mistaken.

clue.text: Posh snack not available in wrap

blocks.note: a cape is a garment you wrap round your shoulders
NA is the usual abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A fancy snack is off the menu when you ask for it in a wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap' pretends to be the tortilla sandwich, which suits the food surface, but it is the shoulder garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapés are small decorative bites served at smart drinks parties, a refined kind of snack.

clue.text: Output a little lower?

blocks.note: surface reading: reduce production slightly
setter's reading: a lower is a cow, one that lows, and its output is a little one, its young

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as more low; say it to rhyme with 'slower' and it is a mooing animal, whose little output is a newborn.
explanation.definitionFit: When a cow gives birth it produces a young one, which is the verb meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Night airs destabilised vessels, we gather

indicators.note: to gather something is to hear it reported, so the words are taken by ear

blocks.note: vessels knocked over, said out loud

explanation.surface: Night winds have toppled some pots, or so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Night airs' looks like breezes; airs are tunes. Say 'knocked urns' quickly and you hear the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a dreamy piece of music evoking the night, as Chopin wrote, so these are evening tunes.

clue.text: Regularly prompt old man

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of prompt

explanation.surface: A father who is always on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' reads as punctual, describing the old man; here it is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop and old man are both informal words for someone's father.

clue.text: Examined origins of surveillance culture with subjective article

an op-ed is a newspaper opinion piece

explanation.surface: Someone studied the roots of the surveillance society through an opinion piece.
explanation.walkthrough: An op-ed, printed opposite the editorial page, is a signed piece of personal opinion, hence subjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To scope something out is to inspect or assess it, so scoped can mean looked over closely.

clue.text: Reference facsimile fooling Yard initially, ensnaring corrupt police

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters count

a snare traps its prey inside it, so one piece encloses another

the six letters of police rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, which suits the crime surface; its F and Y hold a jumbled POLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A file copy is the duplicate kept on record for reference, so it is a facsimile kept to consult later.

clue.text: Proportion and flair backing up the basis of one's argument

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a ratio expresses proportion
élan means dash or flair

explanation.surface: A sense of balance and style supporting the core of a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing up' sounds like supporting the argument; it is an instruction to turn the flair word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the set of reasons underlying a decision, the grounds on which a case rests.

clue.text: Hush hush letters periodically redacted? No!

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of hushhush

explanation.surface: A secret document has its letters blacked out, and someone objects.
explanation.walkthrough: Hush-hush means secret, which is why redaction fits the surface; strike out H, S, H, S and what is left is the refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-uh is an informal spoken negative, a casual way of refusing or disagreeing.

clue.text: Ingredient served up in yakimono dumplings?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down clue, sent upward means read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: A question about what goes into Japanese dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: Yakimono is Japanese for grilled food, keeping the whole scene in a Japanese kitchen; the question mark admits noodles are not really a dumpling filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Udon are thick Japanese wheat noodles, used as a component of many dishes.

clue.text: Dust and mineral aggregate on the beach

indicators.note: to aggregate is to combine things into one total, so the parts are joined together

blocks.note: ash is the dusty residue of burning
ore is rock from which minerals are mined

explanation.surface: Grit and crushed rock washed up along the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aggregate' is a builder's word for sand and gravel, which chimes with the beach, but here it simply adds the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land beside the sea rather than on the water, which is where the beach is.

clue.text: Will Ross love aroused primate?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Will Ross' reads as a question about a person; it is simply eight letters to stir with the O.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow loris is a small nocturnal Asian mammal related to lemurs, so it belongs among the primates.

clue.text: Old volunteers with Oxfam, say, getting letter from NATO

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve before being renamed
Oxfam is an example of a non-governmental organisation

explanation.surface: Former reservists working with a charity receive a letter from the military alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, Territorial Army, is now the Army Reserve, hence 'old'. Oxfam is a British charity. 'Letter from NATO' means the phonetic alphabet, not a posted letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tango is the code word for T in the NATO phonetic alphabet used in radio communication.

clue.text: Staff mid-morning meal starting late unfortunately, one behind time

brunch, a late breakfast, without its opening B
the three letters of one rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club carried by police, a kind of stout stick or staff.

clue.text: Old boy with old English instrument

blocks.note: an OB is a former pupil of a school
OE is the abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy with an antique English musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boy is British for a former pupil; OE is the standard label for the language before 1150.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind played in orchestras, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Prevent fellow in congregation giving way to Bishop

explanation.walkthrough: The church scene makes 'fellow' look like a person; it is just the letter F, which the B replaces.

clue.text: Crush something quickly underfoot – it smells horrible at first

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay also describes the answer: step fast on something foul and that is the sound it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To squish something is to squash it flat, a soft-sounding word for pressing it.

clue.text: More plastic goods provided by this company? Not one!

clue.text: Comedian taking topping off quattro formaggi, perhaps - oddly rude

first and third letters of rude

explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' means cheese on a pizza, but here it is the top letter. Eddie Izzard is a British stand-up comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Izzard is a well-known British stand-up performer, so an example of a comedian.

clue.text: Via telephone, flog basic accommodation

blocks.note: to flog goods is to sell them

explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small plain room for a prisoner or monk, about as spartan as lodging gets.

clue.text: Animal biting worker sent back and tagged again
